marrow__ANAT_CH24_Q012.explanation:
The dorsal nucleus of vagus is present through the floor of the fourth ventricle seen in a cross-section of the medulla at the level of olives.

The following table describes major structures seen in cross-sections at different levels in the medulla oblongata. The trapezoid body and the superior vestibular nucleus are seen in the section of lower pons.

Just inferior to the pons:
• Cavity: Fourth ventricle.
• Nuclei: Arcuate nuclei, inferior olivary nucleus, spinal nucleus of V nerve, dorsal nucleus of vagus, VIII and XI nerve nuclei, nucleus ambiguus.
• Motor tract: Pyramid.
• Sensory tracts: Medial longitudinal fasciculus, tectospinal tract, medial lemniscus, spinal tract of V nerve, anterior spinocerebellar tract, lateral spinothalamic tract.

At the level of olives and inferior cerebellar peduncle:
• Cavity: Fourth ventricle.
• Nuclei: Arcuate nuclei, inferior olivary nucleus, spinal nucleus of V nerve, dorsal nucleus of vagus, VIII, IX, X and XII nerve nuclei, nucleus ambiguus, nucleus tractus solitarius.
• Motor tract: Pyramids.
• Sensory tracts: Same as at the section just inferior to pons.

At the decussation of medial lemnisci:
• Cavity: Central canal.
• Nuclei: Inferior olivary nucleus, nucleus gracilis, nucleus cuneatus, spinal nucleus of V nerve, accessory nucleus, hypoglossal nucleus.
• Motor tract: Pyramids.
• Sensory tracts: Medial longitudinal fasciculus, decussation of medial lemnisci, fasciculus gracilis and cuneatus, spinal tract of V nerve, anterior and posterior spinocerebellar tract, lateral spinothalamic tract.

At the decussation of pyramids:
• Cavity: Central canal.
• Nuclei: Nucleus gracilis, nucleus cuneatus, spinal nucleus of V nerve, accessory nucleus.
• Motor tracts: Decussation of corticospinal tracts, pyramids.
• Sensory tracts: Spinal tract of V nerve, anterior and posterior spinocerebellar tract, lateral spinothalamic tract.

marrow__ANAT_CH24_Q014.explanation:
The given clinical features are suggestive of lateral medullary syndrome or Wallenberg syndrome, which is seen in thrombosis of the posterior inferior cerebellar artery.

The lateral part of the medulla is supplied by the posterior inferior cerebellar artery, a branch of the vertebral artery. Injury or thrombosis to this artery results in lateral medullary syndrome leading to:

• Contralateral loss of pain and temperature on the body — lateral spinothalamic tract.
• Ipsilateral loss of pain and temperature on the face — spinal sensory nucleus of V nerve.
• Ataxia and intention tremors — spinocerebellar tract.
• Vertigo, nausea, vomiting, and nystagmus — vestibular nuclei.
• Dysphagia, dysarthria and hoarseness of voice — nucleus ambiguus.
• Ipsilateral Horner syndrome — sympathetic fibers.
